newsitem.title: JORDAN: Arafat meets King Hussein over Hebron impasse.
newsitem.headline: Arafat meets King Hussein over Hebron impasse.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat met Jordan's King Hussein on Monday to brief him on talks over Israel's long-delayed redeployment in the West Bank city of Hebron.

Jordanian officials said the two leaders held one-on-one talks. They were due to be joined over lunch by delegations including Jordanian Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti and chief PLO negotiator Saeb Erekat.

"We are here to meet King Hussein to discuss our concerns and difficulties about the lack of implementing the accords, which we all signed," Arafat told reporters as he crossed into Jordan from the West Bank at the Allenby Bridge.
"There is still delay and procrastination," Arafat said, adding that Israeli-Palestinian committees discussing security, civilian and economic issues had made no progress.
Neither Arafat nor King Hussein spoke to reporters at the Raghdan Palace in Amman before starting their talks.
Palestinians have been angered by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's delay in implementing the agreement on redeployment in Hebron signed by the previous Israeli government a year ago.

PLO officials said Arafat had rejected a proposal by Netanyahu that they could hold a summit on Monday if Arafat agreed to change the Hebron deal and give Israel powers in areas that were to go to the PLO.
King Hussein, Israel's closest Arab ally since Jordan signed a peace treaty in 1994, has stepped up public support of Arafat in recent days while distancing himself from Netanyahu.
He called on Sunday for a speedy implementation of the Hebron redeployment.
"Peace was in jeopardy and still is, unless these negotiations lead to concrete and conclusive results," he said after returning from a trip to London.

Worried officials say recent violence in Palestinian territories, which killed 60 Arabs and 15 Israelis, raised the danger of chaos on the West Bank spilling over into the kingdom because of close demographic, political and economic links.
